newsitem.title: UK: UK ORR warns of fines over rail enquiries targets.
newsitem.headline: UK ORR warns of fines over rail enquiries targets.

text.p: Britain's Office of the Rail Regulator said on Friday it would fine train operators if they did not improve responses to passengers' enquiries about rail services in the next four weeks.
Rail Regulator John Swift said he was issuing a final enforcement order after warning train operating companies (TOCs) in July about performance standards.

In June, for example, the National Rail Enquiry Service answered only about 51 percent of passengers' calls, meaning that half the people who rang failed to get answers to their queries about train times and fares.
Swift said the service's administrator, the Association of Train Operating Companies (ATOC), had improved performance somewhat since his warning.
"However, although the percentage of calls answered has increased since the figures for April, May and June, too many calls are still going unanswered," Swift said in a statement.
Over the past three weeks, performance levelled off at about 82 percent, below the target of 90 percent.
Swift warned that if targets were not reached between August 17 and September 14, he would impose fines until the goals were achieved on a sustained basis.
He planned to announce soon after September 14 whether he would impose fines under the sliding scale he proposed in July.
The fine scale ranges from 50,000 to 200,000 stg for each percentage point of underperformance. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
